Mali.title: Kenya: Paul Mackenzie and 28 other defendants convicted for the murder of 192 children and one adult
Mali.summary: Bamako, Oct 21 (AMAP) A Kenyan court on Monday found Pastor Paul Mackenzie and 28 other defendants guilty of the murder of 192 children and an adult in the Shakahola massacre, a tragedy that killed more than 400 people, according to Kenyan authorities “I am satisfied that the prosecution has proved the facts against the 29 defendants for the murder of 192 children and one adult in accordance with section 203 of the Criminal Code,” said High Court Judge Diana Kavedza-Mochache when the verdict was delivered.

Mali.title: Image Published on October 21, 2026 Africa Burkina Faso: the death penalty reinstated by the military government of Ibrahim Traoré eight years after its abolition Burkina Faso reinstated, on Tuesday, October 21, the death penalty, abolished in 2018, in a new Penal Code, voted unanimously by the 71 non-member...
Mali.summary: Burkina Faso reinstated, on Tuesday, October 21, the death penalty, abolished in 2018, in a new Penal Code, voted unanimously by the 71 unelected members of the People's Legislative Assembly. The text also toughens penalties for many offences. Archival image of Captain Ibrahim Traoré, at the Second Summit of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) on Security and Development in Bamako, Mali, Tuesday, December 23, 2025 .

Mali.title: MALI: 724 NEW RECRUITS UNDER THE FLAG AT SÉNOU AIR BASE 101, THE 2025 CONTINGENT READY TO PROTECT THE NATION
Mali.summary: The commitment and moral rearmament of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) has reached a new milestone. This Monday, October 19, 2026, the Training Center of the Senou Air Base 101 served as a framework for a solemn takeover marking the end of the Basic Common Training (FCB) for 724 young recruits of the 2025 contingent. A symbolic event of renewal, bravery and dedication to the Fatherland .

Mali.title: Mali: Military Attacks On Civilians, Insurgent Abuses
Mali.summary: Malian armed forces and their allies have since July 2026 responded to mounting attacks by Islamist and separatist armed groups with abusive counterinsurgency operations in central and northern Mali. The Malian military, armed groups, and insurgent forces are committing grave laws-of-war violations while international organizations and governments largely stand by.

Mali.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea Near Conflict; Egypt Forms anti-Ethiopia Coalition; Mali Retakes Kidal: Africa File, October 8, 2026
Mali.summary: October 08, 2026 Ethiopia and Eritrea Near Conflict; Egypt Forms anti-Ethiopia Coalition; Mali Retakes Kidal: Africa File, October 8, 2026 Authors: Liam Karr and Michael DeAngelo Contributors: Alexander Brown and Victoria Hutchinson Key Takeaways: - Ethiopia. Ethiopian federal forces captured the Tigray regional capital Mekele and have advanced north and west toward operationally significant towns, likely spurring Eritrea to deploy a limited number of reinforcements into northern Ethiopia to support the Tigray People’s Liberation Front, although reported Eritrean incursions are unconfirmed.

Burkina Faso.title: Image Published on October 21, 2026 Africa Burkina: Reinstating the death penalty risks being used to "crack down on dissent", according to HRW Reinstating the death penalty in Burkina Faso is a "chilling message" sent to opponents in this junta-ruled country and risks being...
Burkina Faso.summary: Reinstating the death penalty in Burkina Faso risks being used to "crack down on dissent", according to HRW The reinstatement of the death penalty in Burkina Faso is a "chilling message" to opponents in the junta-ruled country and risks being used as "a new tool to crack down on dissent", human rights NGO Human Rights Watch (HRW) warned on Wednesday. . Burkina is led by Captain Ibrahim Traoré, who came to power after a military coup in September 2022.

Burkina Faso.title: Fight against terrorism, Burkina Faso reinstates the death penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: The Government of Burkina Faso had put forward the idea in the Council of Ministers on 4 December. Nearly a year later, the transitional parliament unanimously voted on a new penal code that reinstates the death penalty, although it has been abolished since May 2018. Acts of terrorism, espionage, treason, or even parricide and the import of expired or prohibited products, resulting in death, are punishable by death.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina: the death penalty reintroduced in the Penal Code
Burkina Faso.summary: The People's Legislative Assembly of Burkina Faso adopted, on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the draft law on the Penal Code, thus enacting the reintroduction of the death penalty, which had been abolished in 2018. The draft law revising Law No. 025-2018/AN of May 25, 2018 on the Penal Code in Burkina Faso was adopted on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, by the People's Legislative Assembly .

Burkina Faso.title: Turkish gendarmes in immersion at the national gendarmerie of Burkina
Burkina Faso.summary: A delegation of the Turkish Gendarmerie is staying in Ouagadougou, as part of a working visit and consolidation of the partnership with the National Gendarmerie of Burkina Faso. This mission is led by Lieutenant General Aykut TANRIVERDI, Deputy Commander of the General Command of the Gendarmerie of the Republic of Türkiye . It is with the rise of colors, a highly solemn act and rich in symbols that the Turkish delegation began its immersion within the National Gendarmerie of Burkina Faso .

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: Parliament Votes To Restore Capital Punishment
Burkina Faso.summary: By Enyichukwu Enemanna Burkina Faso’s parliament on Tuesday adopted a revised penal code that reinstates death penalty, nearly a decade after it was abolished in the West African country, the Justice Ministry said in a statement. The revised penal code reintroduces the death penalty for crimes including terrorism, espionage, treason and importing expired or banned products that result in death, government-owned news organisations said.

Burkina Faso.title: Military cooperation: a delegation of the Turkish gendarmerie in immersion at the national gendarmerie of Burkina Faso

Burkina Faso.title: Murders: "Families of victims of crimes, we ask for the lifting of defence secrecy"
Burkina Faso.summary: Below, a forum of victims and members of the secret defense collective, of which the International Network, Justice for Thomas Sankara and his companions is a member. This op-ed is in particular signed by Mariam Sankara, Aïda Kiemdé and Céline Bamouni, respectively daughter of Frédéric Kiemdé and Paulin Bamouni, murdered alongside Thomas Sankara on 15 October 1987 in Ouagadougou .

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: the new Penal Code provides for the reinstatement of the death penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: On Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the People's Legislative Assembly adopted a new Penal Code in Burkina Faso. The text provides for the reinstatement of the death penalty for certain offences, including terrorism, treason, espionage and parricide. The import of expired or prohibited products resulting in death is also concerned.

Burkina Faso.title: Ten suspects arrested in an alleged QNET case
Burkina Faso.summary: The Sangalkam Territorial Brigade arrested ten foreign nationals on Monday, October 19, 2026, in Kounoune Centrale, Senegal, following information indicating the presumed presence of a network linked to QNET. Investigations continue to determine the scope of this network's activities and establish the responsibilities of the defendants The operation carried out by the Sangalkam Territorial Brigade led to the arrest of ten individuals of different nationalities.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: Parliament adopts the reinstatement of the death penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: The People's Legislative Assembly (Alp) unanimously adopted, by 71 votes, the new Penal Code reinstating the death penalty in Burkina Faso. The new Code was passed on 20 October 2026, eight years after the abolition of the death penalty in the country . The Minister of Justice, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, justifies this reform by the need to modernize the legal framework, strengthen security, fight against terrorism and protect populations.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso - The ruling junta reinstates the death penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: - Burkina Faso: La junte au pouvoir rétablit la peine de mort RFI, 21 Octobre 2026 les 71 députés burkinabè ont adopté à l'unanimité, mardi 20 octobre, un nouveau code pénal qui réintroduit la peine capitale… Plus » les 71 députés burkinabè ont adopté à l'unanimité, mardi 20 octobre, un nouveau code pénal qui réintroduit la peine capitale pour un certain nombre de crimes en lien avec le terrorisme, l'espionnage, la trahison ou encore l'importation de produits périmés ou prohibés susceptibles d'entraîner la mort.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: The new Penal Code reintroduces the death penalty for certain offences
Burkina Faso.summary: The People's Legislative Assembly (Alp) unanimously adopted, on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the draft law revising the Burkinabe Criminal Code. Defended by the Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Me Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, the text reintroduces the death penalty for certain offences, in particular those related to terrorism, espionage and treason . Meeting in plenary session, the 71 parliamentarians approved the draft law on the review of Law No.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso adopts a new penal code reinstating the death penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: The death penalty had been abolished in Burkina Faso in 2018 The deputies of the People's Legislative Assembly (Alp) of Burkina Faso adopted on Tuesday evening, unanimously by 71 voters, the draft law on the Penal Code which reinstates the death penalty for certain offences including acts of terrorism and espionage . According to the new penal code, acts of terrorism, espionage, treason, parricide and the importation of expired or prohibited products resulting in death are now punishable by death, explained the Minister of Justice, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, after the vote .

Burkina Faso.title: "Sentimentalism is over": in Burkina Faso, Ibrahim Traoré reinstates the death penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: Eight years after its abolition, the death penalty was reintroduced this Tuesday in the Burkinabe penal code. A security shift assumed by the junta in power, which sees it as a way to fight terrorism and espionage . Burkina Faso reintroduced the death penalty into a new penal code on Tuesday, after a unanimous vote of the unelected members of the People's Legislative Assembly (PLA).

Burkina Faso.title: Military cooperation: Burkina Faso and Türkiye explore new avenues for collaboration between their gendarmeries
Burkina Faso.summary: A delegation of the Turkish Gendarmerie, led by Lieutenant General Aykut Tanriverdi, Deputy Commander of the General Command of the Gendarmerie of Türkiye, makes a working visit to Ouagadougou . The announcement is made this Wednesday, October 21 by the National Gendarmerie of Burkina Faso, specifying that this visit is part of the strengthening of military cooperation between the two countries .

Burkina Faso.title: 66th anniversary of the National Armed Forces: a popular cross-country to kick off the festivities
Burkina Faso.summary: The National Armed Forces organized a popular cross, under the sign of cohesion, as part of the commemorative activities of their 66th anniversary, Tuesday, October 20, 2026, in Ouagadougou. As part of the commemoration of their 66th anniversary, the National Armed Forces (FAN) kicked off activities on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, in Ouagadougou On this occasion, a popular cross-country race was organized in the afternoon that mobilized elements of the Defense and Security Forces (FDS), paramilitary bodies and civilian populations.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso reinstates death penalty: Justice ministry
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina Faso has reinstated the death penalty following a unanimous vote by the country’s unelected legislature, the Justice Ministry announced Tuesday. The new penal code reverses the abolition of capital punishment in 2018. Authorities say the move aims to strengthen public order, uphold national values and improve security.

Niger.title: The Palace Guard Against the Trenches : What the Mutiny in Niamey Revealed
Niger.summary: The mutiny that broke out in air base 101 in Niamey in the night of 29 August 2026 failed. The real question now is to understand why it took place. Those who took up arms against General Abdourahamane Tiani were young soldiers from the front lines, those who fought the ‘jihadists.’ For all of the Sahel, it’s a much more worrying sign than any plot from the army high command.

Niger.title: Military cooperation: Algeria and Niger sign a partnership agreement
Niger.summary: Algeria and Niger want to strengthen their exchanges in the field of defence. This Wednesday, October 21, in Algiers, Chief of Staff Saïd Chanegriha and that of Niger, Salifou Modi signed a memorandum of understanding on military cooperation between the two countries. Said Chanegriha, expressed the readiness of the Algerian army to examine any Nigerian proposal aimed at consolidating their military and security relations .

Niger.title: Agadez: Burial of the bodies of a dozen victims of the armed attack on the Arlit-Agadez axis
Niger.summary: Agadez, Oct. 21 (ANP) – The Governor of the Agadez Region, Major General Ibra Boulama Issa attended, on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, the removal of the bodies, followed by the burial of the victims of the attack against the SONITRAV buses on the Arlit–Agadez axis.

Niger.title: Insecurity: the authorities of Agadez on maximum alert after an armed attack that killed twelve people on the Tchiro-Agadez axis
Niger.summary: The Governor of the Agadez region, Major General Ibra Boulama Issa, chaired an emergency meeting of the Regional Security Council (CRS) on Wednesday, 21 October 2026. Several items were on the agenda of the forum, including, among others, the examination and analysis of the security situation in the region, with a particular focus on the attack on the two SONITRAV buses, which occurred on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, on the Tchirozérine-Agadez.

Niger.title: Niger: two Western hostages released in Libya after more than a year and a half at the hands of the Islamic State
Niger.summary: Niger : deux otages occidentales libérées en Libye après plus d’un an et demi aux mains de l’État islamique Détenues au Niger par l’État islamique pendant plus d’un an et demi, Claudia Abbt et Eva Gretzmacher ont été libérées et sont arrivées à Benghazi. La médiation a été orchestrée par Saddam Haftar, désireux d’asseoir son influence politique au Sahel. C’est la fin d’un long calvaire pour Claudia Abbt et Eva Gretzmacher.

Niger.title: Lieutenant General Said Chanegriha receives the Minister of National Defence of the Republic of Niger
Niger.summary: Lieutenant General Said Chanegriha, Minister Delegate to the Minister of National Defence and Chief of Staff of the People's National Army, receives on Wednesday the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Niger, Lieutenant General Salifou Modi.

Niger.title: Algeria Deploys Military to Bolster Sahel Security
Niger.summary: Algeria’s decision in August to deploy elements of its military to support Niger’s ruling junta was more than simply a policy shift: It showed that one of Africa’s strongest militaries is prepared to project its power in the name of maintaining stability in the Sahel, according to analysts. The day after the Aug. 29 mutiny by a group of Nigerien soldiers, Algeria dispatched four Sukhoi Su-30 fighter jets and an air-to-air refueling plane to Niger’s Air Base 101 in Niamey.

Mali.summary: Forty-eight people were killed in the Menaka region in eastern Mali following an attack by a group affiliated with ISIS, a lawmaker told the Associated Press. Musa Asharatomani, a Tuareg leader and member of the National Transitional Council, said that ISIS fighters in the coastal province attacked the area on Sunday evening and until Monday morning, and the victims included children and the elderly.

Mali.title: Terrorism kills Mali.. 48 people killed in ISIS attacks
Mali.summary: About 48 people were killed in Mali by Daesh members, according to security and local sources. Two security sources and two Malian officials told Reuters that militants linked to ISIS had killed at least 48 people in the country, apparently in retaliation for an attack by government-backed forces including members of Russia's African Legion paramilitary group on suspected informants.

Mali.title: Menaka: at least 48 civilians killed in attacks on camps
Mali.summary: At least 48 civilians were reportedly killed on Sunday, October 18, in attacks on camps near Menaka in northeastern Mali. The Executive Office of the Idaksahak community accuses elements of the Islamic State in the Sahel (ISIS). This violence occurs in the context of clashes between rival armed groups in the region.

Mali.title: Attack by Islamic State-affiliated group in Mali kills 48 people, official says
Mali.summary: AP News

Mali.title: Mali: Violence in the centre of the country - “We fled by canoe in the middle of the night”
Mali.summary: Depuis le début du mois de septembre, le centre du Mali est le théâtre d'une recrudescence des violences qui a fait des dizaines de victimes et provoqué le déplacement de milliers de personnes. Face à ce nouveau flux de déplacés, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) a mis en place une clinique mobile dans la ville de Macina, où converge un grand nombre de familles.

Mali.title: Massacre in Mali: Islamic State attacks the Idaksahak community in the Menaka region
Mali.summary: Massacre in Mali: Islamic State Tackles Idaksahak Community in Menaka Region The Islamic State terrorist attack claimed the lives of at least 48 civilians in the Menaka region of Mali. This massacre, targeting the Idaksahak community and perpetrated in retaliation for military operations, marks a tragic escalation. At least 48 civilians were killed by fighters of the Islamic State in the Sahel (ISS) (ex-Islamic State in the Greater Sahara) on Sunday, October 18, in Tagadayat, in the Menaka region of northeastern Mali.

Mali.title: Mali: more than forty civilians killed Sunday by armed men (security and local sources)
Mali.summary: More than 40 civilians were killed on Sunday in attacks by armed men in the Menaka region of northeastern Mali, causing population displacement, several security, local and associative sources told AFP on Monday. These bloody attacks, carried out by armed men arrived on motorcycles, targeted, according to these sources, several camps belonging mainly to the Daoussahak community, from which the armed movement "Movement for the Salvation of Azawad" (MSA), close to the junta in power in Bamako, came.

Mali.title: Militants Kill 50 Civilians in Mali in Retaliation for 'Azawad Movement'
Mali.summary: ملخص قال مصدر أمني إن المسلحين "أطلقوا النار على كل ما يتحرك، وقُتل 50 مدنياً، بينهم شباب وكبار في السن"، مشيراً إلى أن نازحين فروا من العنف بدأوا بالوصول إلى ميناكا أمس الإثنين، وتحدث مسؤول محلي عن عدد أكبر من القتلى، قائلاً إن الحصيلة "تتخطى 50 قتيلاً، بينهم نساء وكبار في السن". قُتل 50 مدنياً بهجمات شنها مسلحون نهاية الأسبوع الماضي على مخيمات في منطقة ميناكا شمال شرقي مالي، وفق ما أفادت مصادر أمنية وأخرى محلية وكالة الصحافة الفرنسية أمس الإثنين.

Mali.title: Macina hosts more than 3,400 displaced people after the September violence
Mali.summary: RIGHT NOW More than 3,400 displaced people have reached Macina after the violence that occurred in September in several localities in the Ségou region, according to a report published on 16 October by Médecins Sans Frontières. MSF cites an attack in Souleye on September 1 and another in Touara on September 15. The identity of the authors and the complete human toll remain to be established .

Mali.title: More than 40 civilians killed in armed attack in northeast Mali
Mali.summary: More than 40 civilians have been killed in attacks by militants on camps in Mali's northeastern Menaka region, AFP quoted security and local sources as saying. The sources reported that the attackers used motorcycles to reach camps inhabited mostly by members of the Dussaq tribe, whose executive body accused the Islamic State of being behind the killings. According to the sources, the Dussac tribe is the cradle of the armed “Movement for the Salvation of Azawad”, allied with the government, in Bamako.

Mali.title: Mali: more than forty civilians killed Sunday by armed men
Mali.summary: Mali: more than forty civilians killed on Sunday by armed men More than forty civilians were killed on Sunday during attacks perpetrated by armed men in the Ménaka region, in northeastern Mali, causing population displacements, several security sources, local and associative, told AFP on Monday These bloody attacks, carried out by armed men arrived on motorcycles, targeted, according to these sources, several camps belonging mainly to the Daoussahak community, from which the armed movement "Movement for the Salvation of Azawad" (MSA), close to the junta in power in Bamako, came.

Mali.title: Kati: a prayer session in memory of the victims of the crisis
Mali.summary: The Minister of Religious Affairs, Worship and Customs, Dr. Mahamadou Koné, took part, on Sunday, October 18, 2026 in Kati, in a prayer and sacrifice session organized by the military hierarchy in memory of the civilian and military victims of the crisis in Mali . The ceremony was attended by Major General Oumar Diarra, Minister Delegate to the Minister of Defence, military officials and bereaved families.

Mali.title: MENAKA: 48 civilians killed in Daesh attacks
Mali.summary: "At least 48 civilians were killed on Sunday, October 18, 2026, in an armed attack in the locality of Tagadayat, in the region of Menaka". The information was reported yesterday, Monday, October 19, 2026, by the executive office of the Idaksahak community, which attributes this attack to armed men affiliated with the Islamic State group (Daesh). Source: The Renewal Indicator

Mali.title: Defence and Security: 678 young soldiers trained and presented to the flag in Koutiala
Mali.summary: Brigadier General Harouna Samaké, Governor of the Koutiala region, today formalized the end of the training course for 678 soldiers of contingent 2025, in a ceremony marked by the presentation to the flag. After six months of Basic Common Training (FCB), these 678 recruits – out of the 680 initially hired – have successfully completed their course .

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Justice: Opening of the combined hearings of the correctional and criminal chambers of the Military Court of Mopti
Mali.summary: Mopti, October 20 (AMAP) The work of the combined hearings of the correctional chamber and the criminal chamber of the Military Court (TM) of Mopti, for the year 2026, began on Monday, October 19, 2026, at the headquarters of the said court in Sévaré, noted AMAP. Scheduled from 19 to 29 October, these hearings have 43 cases on the docket, involving 72 defendants including 69 military and 3 civilians .

Mali.title: Bamako: two suspects arrested in a burglary case involving more than 200 million FCFA
Mali.summary: The Police Station of the Shopping Center arrested, on the night of October 14 to 15, 2026, two individuals suspected of being involved in several burglaries of shops in Bamako and its surroundings . The operation was conducted under the direction of Chief Commissioner Josué Kamaté, assisted by his deputy, Commissioner Issa Kouma. The investigation, opened following several complaints, made it possible to identify 14 businesses victims of these acts, for a declared damage of more than 200 million FCFA .

Mali.title: More than 40 civilians killed in Mali attack blamed on Islamic State
Mali.summary: Security and community sources in Mali says more than 40 civilians were killed over the weekend in an attack by armed men on camps in the north-eastern Menaka region. They reportedly arrived on motorcycles and targeted camps mainly housing members of the Daoussahak community. The community's executive bureau has blamed the killings on the Islamic State group.

Mali.title: Menaka: Idaksahak community reports 48 civilians killed in Tagadayat
Mali.summary: Menaka: the Idaksahak community reports 48 civilians killed in Tagadayat The Idaksahak community reports the death of 48 civilians in an attack attributed to Daesh elements on Sunday, October 18, 2026, in the locality of Tagadayat, in the Menaka region. Injuries are also reported, according to a statement from its executive office issued on October 19 According to this organization, the attackers arrived on motorcycles and the violence caused many families to flee.

Mali.title: Mali. Human Rights Watch denounces war crimes on both sides
Mali.summary: The American NGO calls on the African Union, which it asks to "take measures to prevent further atrocities. In a statement issued on Monday, October 19, it accused the Malian armed forces and Islamist and separatist armed groups of committing serious violations of the law of war since July “The Malian army and its ally, the Russian-controlled Africa Corps, have killed and injured dozens of civilians in attacks and in detention, in violation of international humanitarian law.

Mali.summary: Published on: Advertisement In Mali, the Executive Office of the Idaksahak community expressed Monday "its strong emotion and immense dismay" after the death of 48 civilians of the community, last Sunday, on the side of Tagadayat, in the Ménaka region According to their statement, "these defenceless civilian populations were attacked by armed elements of Daesh [Islamic State group, editor's note], arrived on board several motorcycles".

Mali.title: Gunmen Kill 40 Civilians in Mali
Mali.summary: More than 40 civilians have been killed in attacks on settlements in Mali’s northeastern Menaka region, with security and community sources reporting that armed men targeted camps over the weekend. The attackers, reportedly travelling on motorcycles, raided several camps largely inhabited by members of the Daoussahak community. The community’s executive bureau blamed the Islamic State group for the killings.

Mali.title: Geneva: Mali celebrates the 66th anniversary of its independence in a spirit of national solidarity
Mali.summary: While in Geneva, Switzerland, as part of the 77th session of the Executive Committee of the Programme of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), the Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralization, Government Spokesperson, Brigadier General Issa Ousmane COULIBALY, chaired the ceremony to celebrate the 66th anniversary of Mali's independence on October 17, 2026 The ceremony took place in the presence of Mali's Ambassador to Switzerland Sékou dit Gaoussou CISSE, surrounded by his counterparts from Burkina Faso and Niger, as well as members of the Malian community based in Geneva.

Mali.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: FAMa strike near Menaka and Douentza
Mali.summary: Operation Dougoukoloko: the FAMa strike two terrorist positions near Menaka and Douentza Thanks to the exploitation of precise intelligence, the Malian Armed Forces carried out targeted strikes on 17 and 18 October 2026 against positions of terrorist armed groups. These operations illustrate the continuation of efforts to monitor, recognize and secure the national territory .

Mali.summary: Mali: more than 40 civilians killed in armed attacks in the Northeast On Sunday, armed men on motorcycles targeted several camps belonging mainly to the Daoussahak community, near Menaka, in northeastern Mali.

Mali.title: 40 civilians killed in attacks on camps in Mali's Menaka region Armed men on motorcycles storm camps housing members of Daoussahak community, killing dozens and forcing residents to flee.

The assailants arrived on motorcycles, storming settlements primarily housing members of the Daoussahak community approximately 50 kilometres from the town of Menaka, in and around the village of Tinabow and the Tagadayat area.

Burkina Faso.title: 66th anniversary of the National Armed Forces: the contribution of the military reserve discussed
Burkina Faso.summary: The Minister of State, Minister of War and Patriotic Defence, Major General Célestin Simporé, chaired the launch conference of the commemorative activities for the 66th anniversary of the National Armed Forces, on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, in Ouagadougou. Burkina Faso's armed forces will blow out on November 1, 2026, their 66th candle . Thus, as part of the commemoration of this anniversary, several activities are on the agenda.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: Government reinstates the death penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: The Burkinabe government officially announced its intention to reinstate the death penalty in December last year. It had been abolished in 2018. “This legislative reform aims to strengthen public order, consolidate the fundamental values of the Nation and ensure the safety of people and property,” the Ministry of Justice wrote in a Facebook post "At the end of the votes, the Alp unanimously adopted the new law on the Penal Code in Burkina Faso," he said.

Burkina Faso.title: Death penalty in Burkina Faso: crimes covered by the new Penal Code
Burkina Faso.summary: Eight years after abolishing it, Burkina Faso is putting the death penalty back into its legislation. The People's Legislative Assembly (Alp) unanimously adopted, on Tuesday, October 20, 2026 in Ouagadougou, a revised Penal Code that replaces that of 2018 . The Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, presented the text on behalf of the government, with the stated objective of ensuring the safety of people and property.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso junta reinstates death penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina Faso’s ruling junta has reinstated the death penalty, the justice ministry said Tuesday, following a unanimous vote by the West African country’s unelected legislature. The new penal code reintroducing capital punishment, which had been abolished in 2018, “aims to strengthen public order, consolidate the nation’s fundamental values and guarantee security for people and property”, the ministry said.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso Reinstates Death Penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina Faso‘s junta has reinstated the death penalty, the justice ministry said Tuesday, following a unanimous vote by the West African country’s unelected legislature. At the head of the military regime that came to power at the end of September 2022 by a coup d 'état, Captain Ibrahim Traoré governs the country with an iron fist.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: the death penalty reinstated by the junta eight years after its abolition
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina Faso reintroduced the death penalty into a new Penal Code on Tuesday, October 20, after a unanimous vote of the unelected members of the People's Legislative Assembly (PLA), which has served as a parliament in the junta-run country since late 2022. The military regime, led by Captain Ibrahim Traoré, had officially announced its intention to reinstate the death penalty in December last year .

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina/Justice: The death penalty reintroduced in the Penal Code, penalties increased
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina/Justice: The death penalty reintroduced into the Penal Code, sanctions revised upwards The Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Me Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, defended, this Tuesday, October 20, 2026 before the parliamentarians of the People's Legislative Assembly (Alp), the bill revising Law No. 025-2018/AN of May 25, 2018 on the Penal Code in Burkina Faso At the end of the votes, the Alp unanimously adopted the new law on the Penal Code in Burkina Faso, with the reintroduction of the death penalty (which had been abolished on 31 May 2018).

Burkina Faso.title: Bobo-Dioulasso: A 13-year-old child dies on a gold mining site abroad, an alleged trafficker arrested
Burkina Faso.summary: Bobo-Dioulasso: A 13-year-old child dies at a gold mining site abroad, an alleged trafficker arrested The Regional Child Protection Brigade (BRPE) of Guiriko presented, on Monday, October 19, 2026, the results of an investigation into alleged acts of kidnapping and trafficking of three minors conducted at a gold mining site in a neighboring country. One of them, aged 13, lost his life .

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger Resume Talks with ECOWAS
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger have reopened formal discussions with the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), more than 18 months after leaving the regional organisation. The two sides agreed on Saturday to set up joint working groups to develop a framework for future cooperation, signalling renewed efforts to rebuild relations. The three countries, governed by military juntas, withdrew from ECOWAS in January 2025 after establishing the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), following military coups and growing disagreements with the regional bloc.

Burkina Faso.title: SCREEN ADDICTION: Everyone is questioned
Burkina Faso.summary: In Burkina Faso, screens have become full members of the family. Phones, computers, televisions, tablets and consoles grab the eyes, swallow the hours and invite themselves into the rooms . WhatsApp, Facebook, TikTok, videos and online games have installed the permanent connection in our concessions and know how to catch us by the eyes and by curiosity.

Burkina Faso.title: AES-ECOWAS: Ministers exchange with diaspora in Dakar
Burkina Faso.summary: AES-ECOWAS: Ministers exchange with the diaspora in Dakar On the sidelines of the first formal negotiations between the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) and ECOWAS, the delegation of the AES met, Sunday, October 18, 2026 in Dakar, with the Burkinabe, Malian and Nigerien communities living in Senegal . The ministers explained the stakes of the discussions with the West African organization and exchanged with their compatriots on the situation in their respective countries.

Niger.title: Fight against drugs in Niamey: 461 people arrested around schools and on the Niger River

Dubbed "Back to school without drugs", this operation allowed the seizure of 7,250 tramadol tablets, as well as diazepam and several quantities of cannabis. The operation took place in two simultaneous phases .

Mali.summary: Hydrocarbon refueling: A third convoy of 734 tanker trucks arrives in Bamako This Saturday, October 17, at around 6 a.m., a new convoy of 734 tanker trucks reached Bamako, escorted by the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa). Mali.title: Sadiola: Four suspects arrested by the police during Operation "Kokadjè"

Mali.title: Refuelling: Bamako welcomes a new record 734 tanker convoy

Mali.summary: After Abidjan's outstretched hand to the ESA countries, the Ivorian intelligence chief is staying in Bamako to relaunch security cooperation. The Ivorian National Intelligence Coordinator, Vassiriki Traoré, is currently in Bamako at the invitation of his Malian counterpart, General Modibo Koné, Director of the National Agency for State Security (ANSE) . On the agenda of the discussions between the two men, the security issue and in particular the fight against terrorism.

Mali.title: Islamic State's military victory over its Al Qaeda rivals in Burkina Faso

Mali.title: Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger: deadly clashes between rival factions in the Sahel of Al-Qaeda and the Islamic State
Mali.summary: Clashes on an unprecedented scale have been taking place for several weeks between the Sahelian branches of the jihadists of the Islamic State (ISIS) and Al-Qaeda (JNIM) in the border area straddling Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger . Mali.title: "Bismillah is darkness", the cult slogan of student demonstrations in France
Mali.summary: It is the story of a slogan, a slogan that we see everywhere, since mid-September, in the demonstrations and blockades of students in France and Belgium as well as on social networks. This slogan, reveals Linda Giguère, is "Bismillah is darkness"! But what does that mean?

Mali.title: Image Africa Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger: deadly clashes between rival factions in the Sahel of Al-Qaeda and the Islamic State
Mali.summary: Clashes of unprecedented magnitude have been taking place for several weeks between the Sahelian branches of the jihadists of the Islamic State (IS) and Al-Qaeda (JNIM) in the border area straddling Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger.

Mali.title: From Mali to Niger, how is Algeria regaining influence in the Sahel?
Mali.summary: Algeria seeks to regain its influence in the African Sahel region through military, security and economic movements, at a time of increasing regional and international competition for the region, with the growing presence of Russia, the UAE and Morocco. Foreign Policy magazine confirmed that Algeria is intensifying its moves to regain its security and military influence in the Sahel and Sahara region, in light of the escalation of security threats and the increasing presence of foreign powers seeking to expand its influence in the region.

Mali.title: Sahel: violent fighting between the jihadists of Jnim and those of the ISE at the Mali-Burkina border
Mali.summary: The Sahelian branch of the Islamic State claims to have killed more than 400 Jnim fighters a week ago in Udalan. A claim published this Thursday in Al Naba, the Islamic State's propaganda newspaper. "The balance sheets of the EIS are always false", tempers a West African researcher, a keen connoisseur of jihadist groups Several specialized sources assure that the deaths are numerous on both sides and that Islamic State commanders in the Sahel were killed by Jnim.

Mali.title: West Africa: Sahel - Violent fighting between Jnim and ISIS jihadists on the Mali-Burkina border
Mali.summary: Since August, there has been significant fighting between the jihadists of Jnim, linked to al-Qaeda, and their rivals the Islamic State in the Sahel (ISIS). These fights are taking place on the border between Mali and Burkina Faso, also not far from the Nigerian border. The last clashes took place at the end of last week, mainly on Friday, October 9 in Gonadaouri, in the Burkinabe province of Oudalan .

Mali.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: the FAMa strike two terrorist positions near Dioura and Tongolo Coura
Mali.summary: Through the exploitation of precise intelligence, the Malian Armed Forces targeted two sites attributed to terrorist groups on 14 and 15 October 2026. These actions are part of the dynamics of surveillance, control and security operations in the national territory . Bamada.net-The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) continue their operations in different theaters of intervention in order to strengthen the security of the national territory and reduce the nuisance capacities of armed terrorist groups .

Mali.title: Sahel: violent fighting between the jihadists of Jnim and those of the ISE at the Mali-Burkina border
Mali.summary: Sahel: violent fighting between the jihadists of Jnim and those of ISIS at the Mali-Burkina border Major fighting has been taking place since August between the jihadists of Jnim, linked to al-Qaeda, and their rivals the Islamic State in the Sahel (ISIS). These fights are taking place on the border between Mali and Burkina Faso, also not far from the Nigerian border .

Burkina Faso.title: West Africa: A war within a war - The clash between JNIM and the Islamic State in the Sahel
Burkina Faso.summary: Ouagadougou — A war within a war. It is the one that takes place in the sands of the Sahara, in the area of the triple border between Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso, where the two main jihadist groups active in the region clash: Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM, Group in support of Islam and Muslims) and the Islamic State in the Sahel (ISIS). The former is affiliated with Al-Qaeda, while the latter is linked to the Islamic State.

Burkina Faso.title: Al-Qaeda and IS rivalry sparks fierce fighting across Sahel
Burkina Faso.summary: Jihadists from rival Al-Qaeda and Islamic State factions in the Sahel have clashed recently on an unprecedented scale in the borderlands spanning Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, with claims of hundreds of fighters killed. The two extremist coalitions, which covet influence over the same areas and control of the same routes and local populations, have repeatedly clashed since 2019.

Mali.summary: In Nioro, elderly people, single women with family responsibilities, people living with disabilities and widows from the El Hadj Omar Tall military camp benefited from donations on Wednesday, October 14. Kits include millet, rice, oil, sugar, pasta and soap . The ceremony, organized as part of the Month of Solidarity and the Fight against Social Exclusion, ended with the presentation of certificates to the sponsors of the thematic weeks and the Month of Solidarity.

Mali.title: Two military operations targeting two armed positions in central Mali
Mali.summary: On Thursday, the Malian army announced the targeting of two sites it said were sheltering armed men, one near the city of Diora and the other in the Ségou area, during two military operations on Wednesday and Thursday, without providing a toll of the losses. The army said in a statement that the first operation targeted a base 12 kilometers northwest of Diora, after being monitored based on intelligence information, noting that it included armed elements and military and logistical equipment.

Mali.summary: The General Staff of the Armed Forces informs the national opinion that the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, are continuing the permanent operations of surveillance, control and security of the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko . Mali.title: Why China won’t build its own Wagner in Africa
Mali.summary: Attacks on Chinese workers in Mali are testing Beijing’s reliance on African security forces. Russia’s experience there gives China little reason to take on the fighting itself. On 9 May, fighters from Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM), al-Qaeda’s affiliate in the Sahel, stopped buses and trucks at Zambougou, in the Ségou region of Mali about 60 kilometres from Bamako, ordered the passengers out and burned at least 40 civilian vehicles.

Mali.title: Mali: The Army announces a tragic incident in an Fama area of operations
Mali.summary: In a statement issued yesterday, Wednesday, October 14, 2026, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Mali said that it had been informed of a "tragic incident that occurred in an area of operations". Mali.title: Dr. Ahmadou Touré: "No sustainable development is possible without effective sovereignty"
Mali.summary: In his new book, "Sovereignty and State Refoundation in Mali (2020-2026): Towards the Alliance of Sahel States", professor-researcher Dr Ahmadou Touré analyses the trajectory opened in 2020. Assistant Professor and Director of the Sahel Governance, Mediation and Security Research Centre, he specifies the criteria for effective sovereignty and the conditions necessary for the consolidation of the ESA .

Mali.title: Kidal: After the army, reinstall the state
Mali.summary: The FAMa took over Kidal on 6 October, almost six months after their withdrawal. Securing the city opens another project: restoring administration, bringing back public services and reconnecting with dispersed populations, while armed groups remain active. The Malian army has consolidated its presence after air and ground operations carried out as part of Operation Dougoukoloko .

Mali.title: Dialogue forum: Civil society and security services meet around the same table
Mali.summary: Representatives of civil society and security actors met this Wednesday, October 14 in Bamako, for the Community Dialogue Forum on Security Sector Governance . Mali.title: 7-October: Benyamin Netanyahu attacked in defamation by the former head of the Shin Beth

Mali.title: NSCDC arrest 2 over abortions, trafficking
Mali.summary: The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) has arrested a 22-year-old man for allegedly trafficking a 17-year-old girl from Kwara State to Mali after promising to secure her employment in Senegal. The command also arrested a 56-year-old man accused of operating an unauthorised medical facility and performing abortions without recognised medical qualifications or a valid licence.

Mali.title: Africa: In Mali, From the Wagner Group to Africa Corps - Will Impunity Continue?
Mali.summary: When Africa Corps officially began operations in Mali in June 2025, few people held out hope that it would help alleviate the suffering of civilians in Mali, caused on the one hand by armed groups in Azawad and members from the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (GSIM), but also by the army and its auxiliaries from the Russian private military company known as Wagner.

Mali.title: National Youth Service: 2,400 recruits of the 7th cohort ready to serve The ceremony of their presentation to the flag was chaired, yesterday, on the place d 'armes of the Military Engineer, by the President of the Transition, Army General Assimi Goïta . For six months, these men and women followed a demanding program of military and civic training that allowed them to learn how to transform fatigue into endurance, difficulties into courage and constraints into responsibilities
Mali.summary: This cohort includes 573 non-public servants and 1,827 civil servants. The 7th cohort of the National Youth Service (SNJ), composed of 2,400 recruits from the first and second waves, completed six months of military and civic training at the Bapho Training Center . The ceremony of presentation to the flag, presided over by the president of the Transition, Army General Assimi Goïta, took place yesterday at the Place d 'Armes of the Military Engineer, in an atmosphere of emotion and patriotic pride .

Mali.title: Mali: At least eight women and children killed by army shelling in Ségou region
Mali.summary: In Mali, at least eight people, mostly women and children, were killed on Monday, October 12, 2026 in aerial bombardments in Zanakoro, a Fulani village in the Ségou region. The Malian army, which is fighting in this part of the country the jihadists of Jnim, linked to al-Qaeda, did not communicate about these strikes. On the images broadcast by the villagers, burnt babies lose their skin by shreds .

Mali.title: Yélimané: three suspects arrested for a fake gold scam
Mali.summary: As part of the "Kokadjè" operation, the Yélimané police station arrested three people on October 9 and 10, 2026. They are suspected of having defrauded several victims by selling them zinc presented as gold After several complaints, the Search Brigade arrested two suspects, I.C., 25, and O.C., 18, on October 9 in Djadji, about one kilometer from Yélimané. According to the first elements of the investigation, they gave zinc to their victims by passing it off as a precious metal.

Mali.title: Zinc Scam Sold for Gold: Three Suspects Arrested by Yélimané Police
Mali.summary: FIGHT AGAINST DELINQUENCY and CRIME: As part of the "Kokadjè" operation, carried out at the instigation of the Regional Director of the National Police of Kayes, the Chief Police Controller Tapa Oury DIALLO, the Yélimané Police Station, headed by the Chief Police Commissioner Adama KODIO, proceeded, between 9 and 10 October 2026, to arrest three (03) individuals suspected of having defrauded several people by masquerading zinc as gold.

Mali.title: Road tragedy at the entrance to Ségou: A young officer loses his life in a three-vehicle collision
Mali.summary: SÉGOU — The national road linking Bamako to the city of Balanzans was once again the scene of a bloody drama on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. A violent collision involving a heavy weight and two light vehicles claimed the life of an Armed Forces lieutenant and injured two others. Bamada.net-Between 11am and 12pm the alert was given .

Mali.title: The UN warns the EU against scrapping international aid in its next budget
Mali.summary: A logo of the UN refugee agency, in Berlin, on June 16, 2022 "A short-termist vision": The UN refugee agency warned against cuts in EU international aid, at a time when Germany is leading an offensive to plan the next EU budget International aid is "an easy target", regrets Jean-Nicolas Beuze, representative in Brussels of this UN agency, the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).

Burkina Faso.title: Autism in Burkina Faso: parents' fight against prejudice
Burkina Faso.summary: In Ouagadougou, parents of autistic children face hurtful remarks and rejection from those around them, in addition to difficulties in finding appropriate support. Ari is 20 years old. Tall, soft-looking, he lives in the Zone 1 district of Ouagadougou.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: Captain Ibrahim Traoré appoints new leaders at the head of the Rapid Intervention Groups (GIR)
Burkina Faso.summary: After the establishment of the Rapid Intervention Battalions (BIR), the Head of State, Comrade Captain Ibrahim Traoré, continued the restructuring of the Burkinabe army with the creation of a new counter-terrorism mechanism: the Rapid Intervention Groups (GIR). In a decree signed on 23 September 2026, he appointed new heads of these units Under the authority of the Special and Rapid Intervention Brigade (BSIR), the mission of the Rapid Intervention Groups (GIR) is to strengthen the operational capacities of the armed forces in the fight against terrorism and organized crime in Burkina Faso.

Niger.title: Niger: an ordinance specifies the missions of the Human Rights Observatory
Niger.summary: The President of Niger, Army General Abdourahamane Tiani, signed on October 14, 2026 an order relating to the National Observatory for Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (ONDH/LF), an institution provided for by Article 72 of the Charter of Refoundation, according to a statement from the General Secretariat of the Government . Responsible for the promotion and protection of human rights, the Observatory will carry out regular, announced or unannounced visits to places of detention, with the exception of the State Security Council.

Niger.title: Niger has set up a National Observatory on Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms
Niger.summary: Niamey, October 14 (ANP)- The President of the Republic, Head of State, Army General Abdourahamane Tiani, signed, on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, an order creating a National Observatory of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (ONDH/LF) . The National Observatory for Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms, it is stated, is an institution provided for in Article 72 of the Charter of the Refoundation and has the mission of protecting and promoting human rights .

Niger.title: Niamey denounces the expulsion of two agents by Paris
Niger.summary: The Nigerien government strongly criticized, on Tuesday, the expulsion by France of two Nigerien agents declared persona non grata on September 16, 2026. Niamey views this decision as a “serious and unacceptable act of ingratitude,” said Justice Minister Alio Daouda According to the Nigerien Minister of Justice, one of the two agents expelled by Paris, Abdoul-Razak Ibrahim Moussa Toro, was wounded in 2014 during a mission to Diffa, in south-eastern Niger, in cooperation with the French army.

Niger.title: Niger: Tebboune strengthens military contacts in the Sahel
Niger.summary: Behind the speech of regional solidarity displayed by Algiers on the occasion of the reception of the Nigerien Minister of Defence, the contradictions of Algerian policy in the Sahel question the real scope of its commitment to regional stability . The reception, Tuesday, October 13 in Algiers, of the Nigerien Minister of Defense by President Abdelmadjid Tebboune comes in a context of recomposition of Sahelian alliances, marked by tensions between Algeria and several countries in the region .

Niger.title: Expulsion of Nigerien agents by Paris: Niamey denounces a "serious and unacceptable act of ingratitude"
Niger.summary: The Nigerien authorities described on Tuesday the expulsion of two (02) Nigerien agents by Paris, in September, as "an act of serious and unacceptable ingratitude" of Macron's France In a statement read on national television, Justice Minister Alio Daouda said that one of the two agents, both "security officers" at the embassy, had been "injured" during a mission to Niger in 2014, carried out in cooperation with the French army, before the break between Niamey and Paris following the events of July 26, 2023.

Niger.title: Weeks after a failed coup attempt in Niamey… Niger's defense minister in Algeria to boost military cooperation between the two countries
Niger.summary: Algeria - “Arab Jerusalem”: Algeria and Niger expressed their desire to strengthen military cooperation between the two countries, in the context of recent developments that contributed to bringing them closer together, including Algeria sending helicopters and military equipment to Niamey, amid Algerian assurances that “the security of the Sahel countries is linked to the national security of the country” This came during the visit of the Minister of State, the Nigerian Minister of Defense, General Salifou Modi, to Algeria, on Tuesday, which was received by Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune and held talks…

Niger.title: “Not Sankara who wants to!”
Niger.summary: “Not Sankara who wants to! The record of Ibrahim Traoré at the head of Burkina Faso and the appointment of Fatima-Ezzahra El Mansouri as the first female Prime Minister of Morocco are on the menu of this African Debate, a program broadcast on RFI in partnership with Jeune Afrique. Published today at 10:11, modified at 10:49 Reading: 2 minutes .

Niger.title: Tebboune receives the Minister of Defense of Niger and discusses enhancing security and military cooperation
Niger.summary: Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune, Minister of Defense in Niger, received General Salifou Modi and his accompanying delegation, according to a statement by the Algerian presidency. The meeting was attended by the Chief of Staff of the Algerian Army, General Said Changiha, Interior Minister Ibrahim Murad, and Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf.

Niger.title: 'Act of ingratitude': Niger condemns expulsion of security agents from France
Niger.summary: Niger on Tuesday condemned the expulsion of two of its security agents from France, calling it a “serious and unacceptable act of ingratitude.” The diplomatic row began last month when Paris declared the two men personae non grata. According to French media reports, their expulsion was related to suspicions they were monitoring Nigerien opposition figures in France.

Mali.title: Reversal of alliances
Mali.summary: The recent bombing of Riyadh International Airport by Yemeni Houthi forces with a dozen dead at the door reflects an implacable truth that the President of Faso, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, has constantly affirmed, namely that "the weak will disappear" .

Mali.title: National Youth Service: The 7th cohort officially presented to the flag by General Assimi GOÏTA
Mali.summary: NATIONAL YOUTH SERVICE: 2,400 recruits presented to the flag The President of the Transition, Head of State and Supreme Head of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi GOÏTA, presided, this Tuesday, October 13, 2026, at the place d 'armes of the 34th Military Engineer Regiment of Bamako, the ceremony of presentation to the flag of the 7th cohort of the National Youth Service (SNJ) .

Mali.title: FAMa: Goïta confirms the recruitment of 2,400 soldiers, including 800 women
Mali.summary: Mali continues to strengthen its defence and security forces, relying on young people to strengthen its ranks. This Tuesday, October 13, Army General Assimi Goïta, President of the Transition, Head of State and Supreme Head of the Armed Forces, chaired in Bamako the ceremony of presentation to the flag of the 7th cohort of the National Youth Service (SNJ) . On the place d 'armes of the 34th Regiment of Military Engineers, it welcomed 2,400 recruits, including 800 women, who are now joining the reserve of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa).

Mali.title: NATIONAL YOUTH SERVICE: 2,400 recruits presented to the flag
Mali.summary: The President of the Transition, Head of State and Supreme Head of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi GOÏTA, presided, this Tuesday, October 13, 2026, at the place d 'armes of the 34th Military Engineer Regiment of Bamako, the ceremony of presentation to the flag of the 7th cohort of the National Youth Service (SNJ) . Composed of 2,400 recruits, including 800 women, this promotion has completed six months of military and civic training and now joins the strategic reserve of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa).

Mali.title: Axis Ségou-Bamako: an accident involving three vehicles killed and injured
Mali.summary: Ségou-Bamako axis: an accident involving three vehicles killed and injured A serious traffic accident involving three vehicles occurred on Tuesday, October 13, 2026 on the Ségou-Bamako axis, between Sébougou and the village of Sékoro. The collision involved a trailer truck, a UNICEF vehicle and a Jeep . According to initial information reported by Sudan Infos, the UNICEF trailer truck and vehicle were heading towards Bamako, while the Jeep was driving towards Ségou.

Mali.title: Sudan: Investigation into a strike that reportedly killed 72 gold miners
Mali.summary: Sudan: investigation into a strike that allegedly killed 72 gold miners The toll put forward by Emergency Lawyers and the origin of the strike have not been independently confirmed. Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan on Monday ordered the establishment of a commission of inquiry after a reported strike in the Jabal al-Uqaydat mining area near the border with Egypt .

Mali.title: THE TITLES OF 13 OCTOBER 2026
Mali.summary: - The trial of Adama Sangaré, former mayor of the district of Bamako, and his co-defendants opened yesterday before the National Economic and Financial Center. They are being prosecuted in the case of the fragmentation of the Bamako-Sénou airport area. - In Kourémalé, near the Guinean border, the death of a young man during a police check provoked the anger of the inhabitants Protesters attacked the police station and blocked the national road.

Mali.title: Ivory Coast-Mali: the boss of Ivorian intelligence expected in Bamako
Mali.summary: Côte d 'Ivoire-Mali: the head of Ivorian intelligence expected in Bamako Faced with the progression of the jihadist threat in the south of its territory and the strategic challenges of the Abidjan-Bamako corridor, Mali shows its willingness to relaunch intelligence cooperation with its neighbor, after several years of tensions . Is security cooperation officially resuming between Abidjan and Bamako?

Mali.title: Mali: Protesters denounce a police "blunder" after the death of a young man in Kourémalé
Mali.summary: The victim is a young man in his thirties, employed as a guard on a gold panning site. Sunday evening, October 11, as he leaves for his motorcycle service, carrying a passenger with him, police officers try to control him. Some sources mention a vignette affair.

Mali.title: Mali: Nduhungirehe, Mali Foreign Minister Discuss Ties, Regional Security
Mali.summary: The Minister for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Olivier Nduhungirehe on Monday, October 12, held talks with his Malian counterpart Abdoulaye Diop in Bamako. ALSO READ: Rwanda, Mali to foster military cooperation Nduhungirehe and Diop discussed regional security and the two countries' bilateral relations and prospects for expanding cooperation in areas of common interest.

Mali.title: Aguelhock, Dioïla and Inafarak: Flood of fire on terrorists As a continuation of the offensive against...
Mali.summary: After confirming the information collected, the site has been processed successfully. The announcement was made on Sunday, October 11, 2026, by the General Staff of the Armed Forces, which emphasizes that the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, continue the permanent operations of surveillance, control and security of the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko .

Mali.title: Mali: Protesters denounce a police "blunder" after the death of a young man in Kourémalé
Mali.summary: Protest movements turned into a riot on Monday, October 12, in Kourémalé, a town on the border with Guinea, after the death, Sunday evening, of a young man during a police check gone wrong. Protesters protested against a new “blunder”, according to them, by the police, after a similar incident last week . The victim is a young man in his thirties, employed as a guard on a gold mining site.

Niger.title: Tebboune receives the Minister of Defense of Niger and discusses enhancing security and military cooperation
Niger.summary: Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune, Minister of Defense in Niger, received General Salifou Modi and his accompanying delegation, according to a statement by the Algerian presidency. The meeting was attended by the Chief of Staff of the Algerian Army, General Said Changiha, Interior Minister Ibrahim Murad, and Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf.

Niger.title: Army General Said Chanegriha receives the Minister of State, Minister of National Defence of Niger
Niger.summary: The Minister Delegate to the Minister of National Defence, Chief of Staff of the People's National Army (ANP), Army General Said Chanegriha, received Tuesday, at the headquarters of the ANP General Staff, the Minister of State, Minister of National Defence of the Republic of Niger, brotherly country, Army General Salifou Modi, indicates a statement from the Department of National Defence (DND).

Niger.title: AGADEZ: The Governor chairs an enlarged meeting of the Regional Security Council
Niger.summary: Agadez, Oct. 13 (ANP) – The Governor of the Agadez Region, Major General Ibra Boulama Issa, chaired a meeting of the Regional Security Council (CRS) in the Governorate's meeting room on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. The meeting of the Regional Security Council was extended to several directorates, including the Regional Directorate of Trade, the SONIDEP Depot Directorate, and the Regional Directorate of Petroleum .

Niger.title: Niger Wrestles with the Aftermath of a Military Revolt
Niger.summary: A mutiny by Niger’s special forces in late August morphed into a coup attempt. In this Q&A, Crisis Group experts explain how the unrest exposed growing discontent within the military’s ranks.

Mali.title: Sahel: Africa Corps hits an armed group with a “Lancet” drone
Mali.summary: The Russian African Corps claims to have struck an armed group using a “Lancet” kamikaze drone, after a camp was detected during an aerial intelligence operation. Indeed, according to the African Corps, the strike hit a hut where there were men described as terrorists by the Russian force. However, the location of the attack and the number of possible victims were not communicated .

Mali.title: Kidal: General Dao announces the continuation of operations beyond the city
Mali.summary: Major General Jean Élysée Dao, Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces, visited Kidal last Saturday and Sunday to assess the security system and pay tribute to the fighters who participated in the recovery of the city. Accompanied by several military officials, he conveyed to them the congratulations and support of the Malian authorities On the spot, he congratulated the heads of the Joint Battlegroups (JTGs) and their men for their commitment to the takeover of Kidal.

Mali.title: Resumption of Kidal: The government has spoken out
Mali.summary: The text stresses that the FAMa, supported by their Russian partners, consolidated their presence in the capital of Mali's eighth administrative region on 6 October 2026. The authorities present this development as the consequence of air-land operations that made it possible to strike the positions of the coalition of opposing armed groups . The government also specifies that after the recent coordinated attacks targeting Malian forces, a tactical redeployment had been carried out around the localities of Anéfis and Aguel-hoc, without questioning the operational presence of FAMa in the region.

Mali.title: Autopsy of a feminoid: A drama that strongly challenges
Mali.summary: This drama is not just about drugs or psychotropic drugs. This tragedy requires the education of boys, the training of families, the strict regulation of firearms and the effective respect of women's right to security and speech in the marital home and Malian society as a whole today, still seriously affected by these repeated femicides. Mali.title: Focus: Kidal: Victory over evil!
Mali.summary: By breaking the supposedly impregnable lock of the Northeast, our valiant soldiers not only erased years of humiliation and terrorist diktat, but they also dealt a mortal blow to the obscurantist hydra that fueled sub-regional instability .

Mali.title: Last minute: The FAMa thwart an attack in Kidal
Mali.summary: As part of Operation Dougoukolo, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, are stepping up their fight to secure the national territory. Mali.title: Reconquest of Kayes in Tinzawatene: Kidal: What remains to be done...
Mali.summary: October 6, 2026 will remain etched as a decisive turning point in Mali's recent history. After days of intense military operations in the North, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their Russian partners, have successfully regained their position in the city of Kidal. This stunning advance is part of the rehabilitation of Operation Dougoukoloko For decades, Kidal crystallized rebellions, fractures, and the state's past inability to fully exercise its authority.

Mali.title: Massive Fuel Flow in Bamako: Over 5,300 Tanks Delivered Successfully!
Mali.summary: More than 5,300 tankers delivered in Bamako since September! This Saturday, October 10, 2026, a new convoy of 957 tankers arrived in the capital, escorted by our valiant Malian Armed Forces (FAMa). The numbers speak for themselves: * September 2026 : 3,796 tankers arrived in Bamako in five convoys, including a record 1,289 tanks .

Mali.title: Sahel: The number of displaced in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger has almost doubled since 2020, according to UNHCR
Mali.summary: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) warns of the displacement crisis in the Sahel: Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger now have nearly 4 million displaced persons and refugees, almost twice as many as in 2020, the year of the first military coup in Bamako . Published on: In Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, “security incidents have nearly doubled since 2020, weakening the state presence […] and increasing risks for both displaced people and host communities,” said Abdouraouf Gnon-Konde, UNHCR's Director for West and Central Africa, on Friday, 9 October .

Niger.title: Suspect arrested over farmer’s killing, kidnapping in Niger
Niger.summary: The police have arrested a 29-year-old man who allegedly contracted kidnappers to abduct and kill a large-scale farmer in Zawudna village, Munya Local Government Area, and took over the deceased’s farmland. The police said Godwin Yahaya was arrested following allegations by rescued kidnapping victims that he conspired with kidnappers to abduct the farmer, Jonah Isah, and others for ransom.

Niger.title: After sending aircraft to Niger… Shangarha confirms that “Algeria does not deal with the crises of the Sahel as an external actor but as an original partner”
Niger.summary: Algeria - “Arab Jerusalem”: The Chief of Staff of the Algerian Army, General Said Shangarha, stressed that Algeria does not deal with the crises of the Sahel as an external actor, but rather as an authentic partner who realizes that the stability of its neighbors is a prerequisite for its stability, in his first comment after the recent developments related to Algeria sending aircraft to help Niger confront a military coup In a speech during his visit to the third military region in the state of Bashar in southwestern Algeria, Shangarha said that Algeria's efforts to help the Sahel countries economically…

The case started with an abandoned motorcycle in the Jacques Chirac district of Zinder .
